notes.title: Caelestia Notes
notes.body:
# Markdown in Caelestia Notes

Welcome to your lightweight **Markdown** note renderer!

> 💡 **Quick Navigation:**
> • **Double-click** anywhere in this note to switch to **Edit Mode**.
> • Press **Esc** or click the **eye icon** in the header to return to **View Mode**.

---

## 📝 Text Formatting

You can format text naturally using standard Markdown syntax:
* **Bold text** using `**bold**`
* *Italic text* using `*italic*`
* ~~Strikethrough~~ using `~~strikethrough~~`
* `Inline code` using backticks `code`
* [Open GitHub in Browser](https://github.com/Denzils-repo/Caelestia_Notes) using `[text](url)`

---

## Persistent M3 Shape Lists

Every list item receives a persistent Material 3 shape that remains fixed across sessions:

### Unordered Lists (M3 Bullets)
- Star shape bullet item
- Cookie shape bullet item
- Sunny shape bullet item
- Gem shape bullet item

### Ordered Lists (Numbered Badges)
1. Read the quick syntax guide
2. Double-click to start writing your notes
3. Enjoy clean, distraction-free markdown

---

## 💻 Code Blocks

```
// Press Esc or toggle the eye button to view rendered output
const app = {
    name: "Caelestia Notes",
    engine: "QtQuick + Material 3"
};
```

---

### 🌐 External Links:
Clicking any external link like [Arch Linux](https://archlinux.org) or [DuckDuckGo](https://duckduckgo.com) will instantly launch your default web browser!

notes.title: Clover's Quick Notes
notes.body:
CachyOS is basically **Arch with extra hype, marketing, and a “2% faster” sticker.**

- **Binary packages:** Recompiled with AVX2/AVX-512, `-O3`, LTO, etc. → ~2% gains in CPU-heavy workloads, which rarely means noticeable FPS gains.
- **Kernels/schedulers:** BORE, EEVDF, sched-ext, etc. mainly target frame-time consistency → usually <1% improvement, while potentially introducing regressions and driver quirks.
- **Cachy repos:** Mostly rebuilds that can cause conflicts for little real benefit. Some are GPU-heavy/broken, and the included scripts solve problems you could easily handle yourself.
- **AUR helper:** Comes preinstalled, which is questionable for beginners since the AUR isn't inherently safe.
- **`-git` packages:** Can break software expecting stable/released versions.
- **Custom kernels:** They *can* help, but can also introduce annoying issues that are difficult to debug—probably not ideal as a default for a “beginner-friendly” distro.

**TL;DR:** Not necessarily bad, just a lot of **“trust me bro, 2% faster”** with extra ways to break things.
